newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares mixed, index up on gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares mixed, index up on gas firm.

text.p: Lithuanian shares were mixed on Tuesday with some blue chips easing but Lithuania Gas and the Lithuania Sea Shipping Company pulled the index up, dealers said.
The Litin A index rose 33.07 points to 2,661.17 and the Litin G index climbed 42.28 points to 2,289.82.
Overall central market volume was over 1.3 million litas and block trades totaled almost 522,000 litas.
Few dealers expected the bourse to really pick up this week but they played down any impact from the expected rise in U.S. interest rates today.
"Domestic investors won't pay any attention to that," said one dealer.
But dealers said that foreign players in the Lithuanian market could respond to the Fed's decision.
"The litas is pegged to the dollar, and if the expected rate hike in the U.S. has an impact on the dollar, it could affect foreign investors here," said one dealer.
"Estonian players in the market pay special attention to that kind of data, especially the dollar's value against the German mark, since the Estonian kroon is pegged to the mark," he added.
The Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company was one of the biggest gainers, rising 9.59 percent to 9.14 litas in trade worth almost 508,000 litas.
Dealers said the market was responding to the company's payment of a hefty 16.5 million litas dividend out of its 1996 net profit of 55.8 million litas.
Lithuania Gas also climbed, advancing to 2.30 litas from 2.29 litas in trade of almost 149,000 litas.
But a number of other A group companies lost ground, including pharmaceutical producer Sanitas, which fell to 107.00 litas from 114.90 litas in trade worth over 28,000 litas.
Dealers said that many blue chip prices appear to be stabilising for the short-term though gains are seen on the horizon.
